title: Per-token autoscale calibrator and int8 dequant fusion path with head-aware kernel routing
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: observed quality regressions and tail-latency spikes for certain customer workloads when using static channel scales for INT8/FP8 quantized kernels and during KV cache reuse. This PR introduces a per-token autoscale calibrator that collects lightweight statistics at runtime and computes per-head multiplicative corrections, a new fused dequantization+matmul microkernel path that consumes the calibrated scales directly, and a head-aware kernel router that prefers low-latency microkernels for heads with tight tail-SLOs. Changes include runtime sampling hooks, a compact in-place scale table attached to the KV cache, a packed int8 microkernel that supports tail-splitting and windowed prefetch, and scheduler hints to prioritize continuous-batching windows where autoscale benefits are largest. Checklist: - [x] design review and perf targets documented (ENG-5783) - [x] unit tests for autoscale state serialization - [x] microkernel smoke tests on x86 and A100 - [x] end-to-end accuracy regression run against standard prompt suite - [x] staged rollout via canary feature flag Implementation notes: autoscale collects per-token max-abs and second-moment approximations over a sliding window (default 256 tokens) with a low-overhead exponential decay; we compress the sliding stats to a single per-head scale multiplier using a clipped geometric mean heuristic to avoid outlier-driven spikes. The scale table is stored alongside KV entries (small 8-byte per-head cell) so that cached prefixes automatically carry their calibrated scale. The fused dequant+GEMM kernel consumes INT8 activations together with a scale table and emits float outputs without an intermediate full-precision buffer, saving memory bandwidth and reducing CPU/GPU kernel launch overhead for small sequences. The head-aware router tags requests with a per-head latency sensitivity score derived from recent p99s and routes hot sensitive heads to the low-latency microkernel, while cheaper heads go to the high-throughput vectorized kernel. Backwards-compatibility: default feature flag disabled for now; rollout plan uses canary on dedicated pools and opt-in via model config. Benchmarks: internal perf lab measured average token latency reduction of 9-14% and upstream throughput improvement of 5-12% on mixed sequence workloads; worst-case p99 improved by up to 23% for customer traces with skewed head activity. Accuracy: end-to-end top-1 divergence against baseline float32 stayed within 0.6% for composition prompts after calibrator clipping; we include automated threshold gating in rollout to detect regressions >1.0%. Risks and mitigations: pathological per-head oscillation was mitigated by the clipped geometric mean and a minimum persistence window; numerical underflow on FP8 paths handled by rescaling heuristic; KV cell size increase kept minimal to avoid capacity regressions. Rollout: canary->50% dedicated->full dedicated->hosted with telemetry gating. Related: builds on previous work for KV-aware prefetch and dequant routing but is orthogonal to prior smoothquant passes and avoids per-weight changes to models.
commits: Add per-token autoscale state and sampling hooks
Implement fused dequant+GEMM microkernel (packed int8, tail-splitting)
Attach compact scale table to KV cache entries and persist through snapshot/restore
Head-aware kernel router and scheduler hint integration
Unit tests, CI config updates, and perf benchmarks
review_thread: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach, can you justify choice of clipped geometric mean vs median? Please add a short note in the design doc.
Maya Chen: Responded: geometric mean matches multiplicative error model we observe for activation scales and offers smoother adaptation; added comparison plots in the design doc.
Priya Nair: Concern about KV snapshot size increase, please quantify impact on dedicated pools.

Maya Chen: Responded: measured average per-KV-entry increase of 64 bytes for 8 heads, typical cache growth <1.2% on 512k entry pools; added mitigation to compress scales for long-lived inactive prefixes.
Ethan Brooks: CI flaked on CUDA 11 build once, reran and passed. Approve pending tiny lints.
ci_summary: All CI checks passed after one retry of CUDA 11 kernel smoke test; performance lab bench suite completed against a/b baseline and canary cluster. Coverage: unit 92%, kernel-smoke 100% on CI harness.
merge_commit_message:
squash: per-token autoscale calibrator + fused int8 dequant GEMM + head-aware routing

Implements runtime autoscale, packed int8 microkernel, KV-attached scale table, and scheduler hints. See ENG-5783 for design.
merge_outcome: merged into main with gated canary flag
release_notes: Runtime: add per-token autoscale calibration and fused dequant+GEMM packed int8 kernel. Improves p50/p99 latency for mixed-length workloads and reduces memory bandwidth for cached prefixes. Feature is behind a canary feature-flag and rolled out gradually.
notes_for_release_engineering: Coordinate canary rollout: enable flag on dedicated-canary pools, monitor p99 and quality gate (0.6% divergence threshold) before expanding to 50%. Rollback: disable canary flag to revert to prior routing; full revert path requires kernel version downgrade.
manual_instructions: To exercise locally: build runtime with KERNEL_PACKED_INT8=1 and run benchmarks/perf/quant_autoscale_mixseq.py with --canary-flag enabled. Use perf tool to capture token-level latencies and /api/internal/telemetry to inspect per-head scales.
follow_up_items: Add GPU memory accounting for per-KV scale cells in telemetry (ENG-5801)
Explore FP8-aware calibrator variant and validate numeric stability (research spike)
Operator tooling: expose per-model scale histograms in Console
